name: Guerneville
tagline: Redwoods, the Russian River and one steep climb
best_months: Summer is when the river town is fully open. Johnson's Beach gives two seasons on its own pages: Memorial Day to October 1 on one, and on its FAQ a 2026 season of daily from June 1 through September 7. The farmers market is listed for June through August. The Russian River floods in winter, so check the roads after storms.
summary: Guerneville is a small Sonoma County town on the Russian River, with redwoods north and the coast west. One loop starts in town: 26 miles over Sweetwater Springs Road, with a 2.3-mile climb at 8.8 percent. We found no bike shop in town; the nearest is in Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line. Cycle to Zero, San Francisco AIDS Foundation's three-day ride, is May 21–23, 2027. Riders camp here two nights, Friday and Saturday, May 21 and 22.
about: Guerneville sits on State Route 116 along the Russian River in Sonoma County, at 59 feet. It had 4,552 people at the 2020 census. It isn't a city. It's an unincorporated community, so there's no city hall. This guide covers the town and the lower river around it. Upriver, that's Rio Nido and Korbel. Just downriver, Guernewood Park and Vacation Beach. Toward the coast, Monte Rio and Duncans Mills. Forestville is to the east. Sebastopol and Santa Rosa are different towns. They're here only for the bike shops and the group rides, because Guerneville has neither.

It's written for two readers. The first is the Cycle to Zero rider. The ride is May 21–23, 2027. Riders camp both nights, Friday and Saturday, at Camp Russian River and Johnson's Beach, about a 15-minute walk apart. Day 2 is about 40 miles or about 100 miles from Guerneville, or a day off the bike. That's the day for coffee and a walk in the redwoods. The second reader is whoever drives up to meet a rider and needs a room. Or anyone who comes to the river with a bike on another weekend.

Know three things before you come. We found no bike shop in town. The nearest is Russian River Cycle Service in Forestville, and it's closed Sunday to Tuesday. One coffee place opens at 6 every day, Coffee Bazaar. Several places to stay are adults only by their own rules. Read the hotel notes before you book for a family. We found no club or weekly group ride that starts in Guerneville. The Santa Rosa Cycling Club starts some rides in Monte Rio and Sebastopol.
riding: Start with the loop from town. The Sweetwater Springs Road loop is 26 miles and about 2,300 feet. It goes north on Armstrong Woods Road, nearly flat, then turns onto Sweetwater Springs Road. The climb is 2.3 miles at 8.8 percent, with short pitches of 16 percent or more. It comes home on Westside Road and River Road past Korbel and Rio Nido. River Road has heavy traffic.

The long days start downriver. King Ridge is 55 miles from Monte Rio. It goes up Austin Creek to Cazadero, along the ridge and down to Highway 1. It comes back through Jenner and Duncans Mills. The Santa Rosa Cycling Club calls it very remote. It counts two water stops in the 40 miles to Jenner. The club's Sonoma Coast loop is 34 miles from Occidental. It passes through Monte Rio, so you can join it there.

The easy one is a drive away. The West County Regional Trail is a county rail-trail, 5.5 miles each way from Forestville through Graton to Sebastopol. It does not reach Guerneville, and no published path links the two. The county's parks department says the river corridor has too few sidewalks and bike lanes and no shared paths. A separate river trail is still a proposal.
getting_there: Drive. Guerneville has no airport and no train. It's on State Route 116 along the Russian River. Sonoma County Airport (STS) in Santa Rosa is the close one, about 10 miles east in a straight line. The drive is longer. Alaska, American, Southwest and Delta fly there. Nine rental car brands have counters in baggage claim (the airport's own pages, 2026). San Francisco International is about 70 miles southeast in a straight line, and Oakland about 69. Groome Transportation runs buses from both to the STS stop, about 2.25 to 2.5 hours, from $39 one way from SFO (Nov 2026). Its FAQ says bikes ride at no extra charge. That gets you to Santa Rosa, not to the river. Without a car, there's Sonoma County Transit's Route 20. It runs between Santa Rosa and Monte Rio through Sebastopol, Forestville, Rio Nido and Guerneville. Every bus has a bike rack. It's a thin schedule. The last bus toward the river that runs every day leaves Coddingtown at 5:20 pm (timetable effective April 12, 2026). The SMART train comes no closer than Santa Rosa.

routes.name: Sweetwater Springs Road loop
routes.surface: Paved. Patchy and bumpy on the Sweetwater Springs descent along Porter Creek.

start.name: Downtown Guerneville (the route page suggests street parking on First Street, one block off River Road)

routes.description: The loop that leaves from town. North on Armstrong Woods Road, nearly flat, to the redwood reserve. Then right onto Sweetwater Springs Road: narrow, twisting, almost no cars, and one hard climb. Down the far side to Westside Road and its wineries, then River Road back past Korbel and Rio Nido. Ride it clockwise; the other direction opens with a quarter mile over 16%. The route page dates from 2010, so expect the pavement and the parking signs to have changed. Coffee Bazaar, the 6 a.m. coffee, and boon hotel + spa are both on Armstrong Woods Road. That's the road the loop goes out on.
routes.hazards: The climb is 2.3 miles at 8.8% with short pitches of 16% or more; the route page's author walked the worst of it. The descent after it is steep, narrow and curvy on patchy pavement. Westside Road's shoulder is 1 to 2 feet and sometimes gone. River Road back to town has heavy traffic.

routes.name: West County Regional Trail
routes.surface: Bike path, mostly paved. A boardwalk north of Graton and compacted rock near Ross Station Road.

start.name: Forestville trailhead, Highway 116 in downtown Forestville (parking)

routes.description: The easy one. A county rail-trail from downtown Forestville south through Graton to Sebastopol, 5.5 miles each way. That's 11 out and back. Free parking at the Forestville, Ross Station Road and Graton Road trailheads. In Sebastopol it meets the Joe Rodota Trail, 8.5 more miles to Santa Rosa; the county counts 14 miles for the pair. Open 7 a.m. to sunset. It does not reach Guerneville. Forestville is about 6 miles east of it in a straight line. Russian River Cycle Service, the nearest bike shop to Guerneville, is at the Forestville trailhead.
routes.hazards: Shared with walkers, dogs and joggers. A club route that uses it warns of a dirt section and posts on the Graton stretch. If you carry on along the Joe Rodota Trail, the county says the crossings at Merced Avenue and Llano Road are unimproved and need care.

routes.name: Sonoma Coast
routes.description: The coast loop, from the Santa Rosa Cycling Club's Ten Great Rides. Down the Bohemian Highway along Dutch Bill Creek to Monte Rio. Moscow Road along the river to Duncans Mills, then Highway 116 to Jenner. About 10 miles south on Highway 1. Bay Hill Road, Bodega, Joy Road and Bittner Road bring it back to Occidental. A rider staying in Guerneville can join it where it passes through Monte Rio. The club's page names a bakery and coffee at the Duncans Mills bridge (about mile 10). It names a coffee shop across from the Bay Hill junction (about mile 22). The Blue Heron tavern is in Duncans Mills too.
routes.hazards: River Road (Highway 116) between Duncans Mills and Jenner has heavy traffic and shoulders that come and go. Highway 1 backs up on summer and holiday weekends. Bay Hill climbs about 750 feet in 1.5 miles. Joy Road has two steep climbs back to back. The Coleman Valley alternate descends steep and twisting, with cattle guards, potholes and sudden drop-offs. The Bohemian Highway descent is cold in the morning. Riding to Monte Rio from Guerneville on Highway 116 means the one-lane zone with temporary signals between Sheridan Ranch Road and Vacation Beach, expected into early 2027 (Caltrans, July 30, 2026).

routes.name: King Ridge
routes.surface: Paved. Old rough pavement on Austin Creek Road, mediocre to very bad on the Hauser Bridge descent, smooth on Meyers Grade.

start.name: Parking lot at the north end of the Russian River bridge, Monte Rio

routes.description: The big one, and one of the Santa Rosa Cycling Club's Ten Great Rides. Up Austin Creek to Cazadero, onto King Ridge Road and its open ridgetop, then down Hauser Bridge Road. Back over Seaview and Meyers Grade to Highway 1. Then Jenner, Duncans Mills and Moscow Road home. The club calls it very remote and says only fit, self-reliant riders should try it. A Fort Ross Road shortcut makes it 36 miles and it is still hilly. The club's page gives no total for the climbing.
routes.water: Cazadero general store (mile 9). After that the club counts two refills in the 40 miles to Jenner: a hose bib at Ratna Ling Retreat Center (mile 28.6) and Fort Ross Elementary School (mile 32.8). Jenner has a small store and water in the park across the street. Bakery and café in Duncans Mills (about mile 51). The club's page carries no date, so don't count on any one of them.
routes.hazards: Hauser Bridge Road drops for a mile and ends in a 20% pitch onto a one-lane iron-grate bridge, with loose gravel, potholes and tree roots. Meyers Grade is a 16% descent to Highway 1. Cattle guards on the ridge roads. Highway 1 and River Road (Highway 116) carry real traffic, and River Road often has no shoulder. Long stretches with no services. Fog on the ridge; dress for a cold start. Riding to the start from Guerneville on Highway 116 means the one-lane zone with temporary signals between Sheridan Ranch Road and Vacation Beach, expected into early 2027 (Caltrans, July 30, 2026).

routes.name: Howarth to Korbel (clockwise)
routes.surface: Mixed: paved roads and paved multi-use trails, with some gravel, dirt and rough pavement (rough on Old River Road).

start.name: Lower tennis court parking lot, Howarth Park, Santa Rosa (free parking)

routes.description: A Santa Rosa Cycling Club ride leader's loop, published as a RideWithGPS ambassador route. It goes from Santa Rosa out to the deli at Korbel, just upriver of Guerneville, and back. Out on the Santa Rosa Creek and West County trails through Graton and Forestville, then Martinelli Road and River Road. Home by Westside Road, Wohler Bridge and Eastside Road. It is the published way to link the river and Santa Rosa mostly off the main roads. It starts in Santa Rosa, so it's for a visitor based there or driving in. Graded hard on distance alone; the steepest hill is an eighth of a mile at up to 9%.
routes.water: Korbel Deli (coffee, sandwiches). Gas station and minimart at Occidental Road and Gravenstein Highway, with a restroom. Roasters Espresso Bar in Forestville. Portable toilet in the lot before Wohler Bridge.
routes.hazards: River Road is busy and its shoulder collects debris. Gravel on the turn onto Eastside Road has put riders down. A sharp right onto Sunset Avenue drops straight into a descent. The trails are crowded; slow for the underpasses at Stony Point and Fulton. Heavy traffic on Guerneville Road coming back into Santa Rosa.

coffee.name: Coffee Bazaar
coffee.note: Downtown, on Armstrong Woods Road, the road the Sweetwater Springs loop goes out on. Opens at 6 every day, Saturday and Sunday included, so it's the one that's open before a morning ride. Sonoma County Tourism's listing says outdoor seating; the café's own site doesn't mention it, and nothing says bike parking. Listings differ on closing time, and the café's site dates from 2024. Call about the afternoon: (707) 869-9706. Russian River Books & Letters is at the same address.
coffee.hours_hint: 6 a.m. daily; closes 4 p.m. Monday to Thursday and 6 p.m. Friday to Sunday by its own site; one listing says 5 p.m. daily

coffee.name: The Farmhand
coffee.note: A deli, espresso bar and market on River Road, the road the Sweetwater Springs loop comes back to town on. Opens at 9, so it's for after the ride. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday (its own site, Nov 2026). Sonoma County Tourism's listing says outdoor seating. Nothing says bike parking.
coffee.hours_hint: Friday to Monday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Thursday 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.; closed Tuesday and Wednesday (its own site, Nov 2026)

restaurants.name: Piknik Town Market
restaurants.note: Breakfast and lunch on Main Street: a market with baked goods, salads and grab-and-go food. Opens 8 a.m. every day; closes 5 p.m. Saturday and 4 p.m. the other six (its own page, Nov 2026). Its page says nothing about tables, inside or out. (707) 604-7295.

restaurants.name: Guerneville Taco Truck
restaurants.note: Tacos, burritos and a breakfast burrito from a truck in town. Good for the night before. Open daily 11:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. (its own page, Nov 2026). The page gives no prices, seating or payment details; Sonoma Magazine says cash only, so bring some. Other listings give other addresses for it, so check it's parked there before a group walks over.

restaurants.name: Stumptown Brewery
restaurants.note: A brewpub on River Road, the road the Sweetwater Springs loop comes back to town on. It's the late one. The kitchen runs 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. Sunday to Thursday and to 10 Friday and Saturday. The pub opens at 11 a.m. every day and stays open until at least 11 p.m. (its own pages, Nov 2026). That's the latest kitchen we found in town. Its site describes a "huge deck overlooking our 2 acre river front." It says nothing about bikes. The site is old, so call first: (707) 869-0705.

restaurants.name: The Lodge at Dawn Ranch
restaurants.note: A sit-down breakfast, and a dinner for the people who drove up. Breakfast 8 to 11 a.m. Monday to Friday, brunch 8 a.m. to noon Saturday and Sunday. Dinner from 5 p.m., last seating 8 Thursday, Sunday and Monday and 8:30 Friday and Saturday; no dinner Tuesday or Wednesday (its own page, updated Sept 2026). Book dinner: the page says reservations are strongly recommended. It's the restaurant at Dawn Ranch, the resort. (707) 869-0656.

restaurants.name: boon eat + drink
restaurants.note: A small bistro on Main Street with seasonal plates, a burger and a vegan bowl. Dinner only, from 4 p.m.: to 8 Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday, to 9 Friday and Saturday; closed Monday and Tuesday (its own page, Nov 2026). No reservations and walk-in parties of six at most, so a big group splits up or goes elsewhere. Mains $26–$45 (Nov 2026). 707-869-0780.

restaurants.name: Blue Heron Restaurant and Tavern
restaurants.note: A tavern with a seafood kitchen in Duncans Mills, where the King Ridge and Sonoma Coast routes both pass. The patio has music on Sundays. The kitchen runs 4:30 to 8 p.m. Tuesday to Friday, noon to 8 Saturday and noon to 7 Sunday; no kitchen hours are posted for Monday. The bar is open daily, from 3 p.m. on weekdays and noon on weekends, to 10 (its own page, Nov 2026). Groups of eight or more need a reservation. (707) 865-2261.

hotels.name: boon hotel + spa
hotels.note: Fourteen rooms on Armstrong Woods Road, the road north to the redwood reserve. The Sweetwater Springs loop goes out this way. "21+ adults-only," by its policies page. It has house bikes for guests, in its own words: "We have cruiser bikes available complimentary to our guests." Queen rooms have "private back decks." Saline pool and hot tub. Check-in 3 pm, 14-day cancellation. Nothing about bringing your own bike. Check the site for rates.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: Dawn Ranch
hotels.note: Cabins, chalets, cottages, bungalows and glamping tents on the river; "Our property stretches along the banks of the Russian River." It has house bikes for guests, in its own words: "Explore the town of Guerneville and the surrounding countryside with our complimentary fleet of Retrospec bikes." One chalet is ADA-compliant with a ground-level king bed. Restaurant and spa on site. Nothing about bringing your own bike, and nothing on children or minimum stays on its pages. Check the site for rates.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: The Stavrand Russian River Valley
hotels.note: Twenty-one rooms in three houses on Highway 116. A hot plated breakfast for two is included. Pool, free parking and a desk staffed around the clock. Its FAQ says "We welcome families with children." It has house bikes for guests, in its own words: "Take out one of our cheerful yellow bicycles for a spin (first-come, first-served)." Rooms in the Cazadero house have "direct access to our surrounding nature"; ask for one if the bike is coming. Nothing about bringing your own bike. Check the site for rates.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: The Woods
hotels.note: Cottages and cabins around a pool in the middle of town; its page says it is "within walking distance to shops, restaurants, dancing and live entertainment." In its own words: "Gay-owned," and "an adult-hotel and not recommended for minors." Its chamber listing calls the pool clothing optional; the hotel's policies page doesn't say, so ask. "Room rates span $175.00 to $510.00" plus 14% tax (read Nov 16, 2026). Its policies say "There is a 2 night minimum on weekends during high season more for holiday and special events." Nothing about bikes.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: The Highlands
hotels.note: Cabins, suites and small studios in the redwoods, "a short walking distance to downtown Guerneville" by its own page. Adults only: "All guests must be at least 18 years old." Its policies say the pool is "NO longer clothing optional." Book early for an event weekend: "2 night minimum stay on weekends" and "Special Event and Holiday Weekends often have 3-5 night minimum stays." Its outdoors page points guests to a rental outfit that delivers bikes; nothing about bringing your own. Check the site for rates.
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

hotels.name: Cottages on River Road
hotels.note: The cheap one, and the one for the family who drove up. Studios and cottages on River Road; its own page says it is "across the street from the river," Korbel is "5 minutes" away and Armstrong Woods "a 12 minute drive." Every unit lists a "Patio & Seating Area," a mini-fridge and a coffee maker; there is free parking, pay laundry and a continental breakfast. Quiet hours start at 10 pm. Nothing about bikes beyond "biking the back roads." Queen Studio $79–$219 a night on its own page (read Nov 16, 2026).
hotels.bike_policy: No stated policy — ask when you book

bike_shops.name: Russian River Cycle Service
bike_shops.note: In Forestville, about 6 miles east of Guerneville in a straight line, at the trailhead of the West County Regional Trail. The nearest shop to Guerneville; we found none in town. A one-person repair shop: small jobs often while you wait, simpler ones usually by the end of the day, never over a week. Open Wednesday to Friday 11 to 6 and Saturday 9 to 5; closed Sunday to Tuesday, with rental appointments seven days a week. Road bikes $75 a day, hybrids $45 (Nov 2026). The rental page names no brand or sizes, so call and ask what the bike is.

bike_shops.name: Revel Cycles
bike_shops.note: In The Barlow in Sebastopol, about 12 miles southeast of Guerneville in a straight line. Open every day 11 to 6, so it covers Sunday to Tuesday, when the Forestville shop is closed. It prints its prices: tune-up $150, flat repair $20, basic fit $95, packing a bike for travel or shipping $125, building a bike from the box $200 (Nov 2026). Rentals are e-bikes ($75 for 3 hours, $95 a day) and cruisers ($50 a day). No road, gravel or mountain bikes to rent.

bike_shops.name: Trek Bicycle Santa Rosa
bike_shops.note: In downtown Santa Rosa, about 16 miles southeast of Guerneville in a straight line. Says it turns most service around in 24 hours on any brand, no appointment needed. Boxes a bike for travel for $79.99 (Nov 2026). Closed Mondays; Tuesday to Friday 11 to 6, Saturday 10 to 6, Sunday 12 to 5. No rentals listed.

bike_shops.name: Sports Basement Santa Rosa
bike_shops.address: 1970 Santa Rosa Avenue, Santa Rosa, CA 95407
bike_shops.note: In Santa Rosa, about 16 miles southeast of Guerneville in a straight line. The widest rental range near the river: carbon road bikes $100 a day or $175 for 2 to 4 nights, aluminum road $75 a day, deposit required (chain rates, Nov 2026). Open Monday to Friday 10 to 7, Saturday and Sunday 9 to 6. The chain's service page says many small jobs are done on the spot. It builds a bike from its box for $155 and boxes one for shipping for $110 (Nov 2026). The pages don't say which models and sizes are in Santa Rosa, so reserve ahead.

culture.name: Johnson's Beach
culture.note: The river beach in the middle of town. In season: canoes, kayaks, tubes, chairs and umbrellas to rent from 10 am (back by 5), and a snack shack from 11 to 5 with beer and wine until 6. Parking is $10 a car for day visitors (read Nov 2026); no pets, no outside alcohol. It's seasonal, and its own pages give two seasons. One says it opens on Memorial Day and closes October 1. Its FAQ had the beach open one weekend in mid-May 2026, then daily from June 1 through September 7. No 2027 dates are posted (read Nov 2026). Memorial Day 2027 is May 31, so don't count on the beach, the rentals or the snack shack in May.

culture.name: Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve
culture.note: Old redwoods north of town, at the end of Armstrong Woods Road. Open 8 am to an hour after sunset. The Pioneer Nature Trail is about 1.5 miles round trip and mostly flat; the Parson Jones Tree, over 310 feet, is a tenth of a mile from the entrance. $10 a vehicle (Nov 2026); the page doesn't say what a walker or a rider pays. Bikes stay on the main paved road and one fire road. The park's page listed the East Ridge Connector Trail closed and Austin Creek camping closed (alerts dated Nov 1, 2026).

culture.name: Russian River Books & Letters
culture.note: The town's bookstore, at the same address as Coffee Bazaar. Fiction, memoir, kids' books, Spanish-language and LGBTQ+ shelves, plus readings and a book club. Opens at 10 every day but Tuesday, when it's closed; shuts at 5, or 7 on Fridays and Saturdays through the end of 2026 (chamber listing, Oct 2026). A stop for after the ride.

culture.name: Rainbow Cattle Company
culture.note: A saloon on Main Street, open since 1979 and started for gay visitors to the river, by its own site. Locals call it the Rainbow or the Bow, by the county tourism listing. Hours aren't on its site or the listings, so call (707) 869-0206.

culture.name: Russian River Art Gallery
culture.note: A co-operative gallery of Sonoma County artists on Main Street: paintings, photography, ceramics, jewelry, cards. Twenty minutes, not two hours. Its site gives summer hours of 11 to 6, closed Wednesdays, and winter hours of 11 to 5, closed Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov 2026). It doesn't say when one becomes the other, so call (707) 869-9099.

culture.name: Guerneville Certified Farmers Market
culture.address: Fourth and Church Streets, Guerneville, CA 95446
culture.note: Listed for Thursdays, 3 to 7 pm, June through August only, behind Hubert's Hall downtown (chamber and county tourism listings, Nov 2026). Produce, baked goods and food made to order, with outdoor seating. Not listed for May or the rest of the year. Neither listing gives 2027 dates, so check before you plan around it.

clubs.name: Santa Rosa Cycling Club
clubs.note: The county's big road club, and the one whose calendar reaches the river. Rides most days at 9:30 am from parks in Sebastopol, Windsor, Healdsburg and Santa Rosa, and some from Monte Rio and Graton. In November 2026 its calendar had a ride from Sebastopol to Guerneville and two coast rides from the Monte Rio Community Center. Each listing gives a terrain number, a pace letter and the miles. A non-member can ride once after signing the waiver at the start; after that you join ($25 a year, or a free 90-day trial, read Nov 2026). The King Ridge and Sonoma Coast routes in this guide are the club's.

clubs.name: Sports Basement Santa Rosa
clubs.note: A shop that leads a free road ride from inside the store at 1970 Santa Rosa Ave. Most routes are 30 to 40 miles and nobody is left behind. Show up; the shop posts changes on its Strava club. Day and time: {ride:santa-rosa-ca-sports-basement-last-sunday-ride|the shop's no-drop ride}. It's in Santa Rosa, about 16 miles southeast of Guerneville in a straight line.

clubs.name: Santa Rosa Taco Tuesday Ride
clubs.note: A community evening ride through central Santa Rosa to the taco trucks at Mitote Food Park and back, 8 miles round trip, all year. Free, show up. Rain and holidays cancel it. Worth it if you're already in Santa Rosa on a Tuesday; not a reason to drive from the river.

bring_your_bike.summary: Bring it if you are staying more than a day or two, and plan on a car. We found no bike shop in Guerneville. The nearest is a repair and rental shop in Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line. The widest rental fleet is in Santa Rosa, about 16 miles off. The airport is close: Sonoma County (STS), about 10 miles east in a straight line. American, Delta and Southwest all check a packed bike at the standard bag fee (Nov 2026). No shop near the river says it takes a shipped bike.

airports.name: Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport
airports.note: The close one, about 10 miles east in a straight line; the drive is longer. Four airlines fly here, by the airport's passenger FAQ (modified Oct 9, 2026). Alaska: Boise, Burbank, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Orange County, Palm Springs, Phoenix, Portland, San Diego, Seattle. American: Phoenix, Dallas-Fort Worth. Southwest: Denver, Burbank, San Diego, Las Vegas. Delta: Salt Lake City. Nine rental car brands on site, counters in baggage claim: ACE, Avis, Budget, Enterprise, Hertz, National, NextCar, Dollar, Thrifty (the airport's car-rental page). The curb in front of the terminal is the pick-up zone. The airport's pages say nothing about bikes, oversized bags or any service to Guerneville. 2200 Airport Boulevard, Santa Rosa; (707) 565-7243.

airports.name: San Francisco International
airports.note: About 70 miles southeast in a straight line. Groome Transportation runs 17 buses a day each way between SFO and Sonoma County, about 2.25 to 2.5 hours to the STS stop, from $39 one way (Nov 2026). Its FAQ says it takes bicycles at no extra charge and asks riders to limit their luggage. It doesn't say whether that means a boxed bike, so call ahead with a case. That gets a bike to Santa Rosa, not to the river.

airports.name: Oakland International
airports.note: About 69 miles southeast in a straight line. Groome runs 7 buses a day each way between OAK and Sonoma and Marin counties, about 2.25 hours to the STS stop, $55 one way (Nov 2026), on minibuses. Same bike line in its FAQ.

fly.airline_note: From each airline's own page, Nov 2026, unless marked. American: one non-motorized touring, mountain, tandem or racing bike in a hard case, a bike bag or a box built for bikes; standard checked bag fee up to 50 lb, standard overweight fee from 50 to 70 lb, oversize fees do not apply; not in a hard case it is treated as fragile. Main Cabin first bag $45 online or $50 at the airport, second $55 or $60, for tickets issued on or after April 9, 2026; Basic Economy $50 or $55, second $60 or $65, for tickets from May 18, 2026; overweight $30 for 50 to 53 lb and $100 for 53 to 70 lb. Southwest: a non-motorized single-seat bike is checked baggage at standard bag and overweight fees, oversize waived; over 100 lb or 115 inches is refused; pedals and handlebars off and wrapped; cardboard or a soft case flies on a limited release. First bag $45, second $55 on Basic, Choice and Choice Preferred fares; 51 to 70 lb adds $100. Delta: a non-motorized touring or single-seat racing bike in a container built for bikes goes at the standard bag allowance and fee; over 50 lb pays an excess weight fee the page does not price; 100 lb or more, or over 115 linear inches, is refused; a hard-shell bike case needs no release, a soft bag signs one; some Delta Connection flights exclude bikes. First bag $45, second $55, US domestic Main. Alaska flies the most routes into STS. Alaska (Sept 2026): a cased bike is a standard checked bag, oversize waived and overweight waived to 70 lb, first bag $45, second $55; read its sports-equipment page before you book. Keep the case under 50 lb and it is one ordinary checked bag on American, Southwest and Delta.

ship.note: No shop within reach of Guerneville says on its own site that it receives a shipped bike (Nov 16, 2026). Three will build one you bring in a box, or pack yours to go home, for a published fee. Revel Cycles in Sebastopol builds a bike from the box for $200 and packs one for $125; Sports Basement builds one from its box for $155 and boxes one for $110; Trek Bicycle Santa Rosa boxes one for $79.99 (Nov 2026). Russian River Cycle Service in Forestville is the nearest shop; its site says repair and rentals and nothing about shipping, boxing or assembly. Call (707) 887-2453 before you send anything, and note it is open Wednesday to Saturday only. BikeFlights ships by UPS and its help page gives no transit-day count. If a shop agrees to take it, ship at least a week ahead. Flying into STS with the bike is the simpler way.

rent.note: We found nothing to rent in Guerneville itself; the county tourism office's bike-rental list has no Guerneville or Monte Rio entry. The nearest road bikes are in Forestville; the widest choice is in Santa Rosa. The math: a cased bike is $45 each way on American, Southwest or Delta, so about $90 round trip (Nov 2026). Sports Basement's alloy road bike is $75 for a day, $135 for two to four days and $220 for a week, so renting wins for a one-day ride and for anyone driving up without a bike, and it is close to even for a long weekend. For a week, for a fit you depend on, or for gravel, bring yours: the Santa Rosa store's page doesn't name gravel bikes. Sports Basement also rents a hard bike travel case ($55 a day, $80 for two to four days, $110 a week), which helps a rider flying home.

shops.name: Russian River Cycle Service
shops.note: Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line. Road bike $75 a day with a helmet and repair kit; hybrid $45 a day with helmet, basket, lock and pump (Nov 2026). The page gives no brand, frame, groupset or sizes: tell them your pedals and ask what the bike is. Rental appointments seven days a week; delivery offered.

shops.name: Sports Basement Santa Rosa
shops.note: Santa Rosa, about 16 miles southeast in a straight line. Chain rates (Nov 2026): carbon road $100 a day, $175 for 2 to 4 nights, $300 for 5 to 9; aluminum road $75 a day; full-suspension carbon mountain bike $135 a day; e-bike $75 a day. Deposit required. Reserve online ahead; same-day in store with a smaller choice.

shops.name: Revel Cycles
shops.note: Sebastopol, about 12 miles southeast in a straight line. E-bikes $75 for 3 hours or $95 a day; cruisers $50 a day (Nov 2026). Free cancellation up to 24 hours ahead. No road, gravel or mountain bikes.

get_around.note: Yes, for most visitors. We found no train and no airport shuttle to Guerneville. The nearest bike shop is about 6 miles east in a straight line, and the widest rental fleet is about 16 miles away in Santa Rosa. With a bike case, rent a car at STS (nine brands in the terminal) or book a large rideshare; a bus rack takes a built bike, not a box. With a built bike and no car it can be done. Sonoma County Transit's Route 20 runs between Santa Rosa and Monte Rio through Sebastopol, Forestville, Rio Nido and Guerneville. Every bus has racks, and it stops on 3rd Street near the Railroad Square SMART station. It is a thin schedule. It's one daily timetable with some weekday-only trips. Toward the river, the last bus that runs every day leaves Coddingtown at 5:20 pm (Route 20 timetable, effective April 12, 2026). Once you are in town with a built bike, downtown and the river are rideable; the roads out are the question, and that is in the rules and safety line. Caltrans has one-way signal control on Highway 116 west of town, between Sheridan Ranch Road and Vacation Beach, expected to last into early 2027 (advisory of July 30, 2026).
get_around.transit_bike_rules: Sonoma County Transit (its bike page, Nov 2026): every bus has a front rack for two or three bikes, first come, first served, no extra fare. A bike can be up to 80 inches long, 48 tall and 24 wide. Standard two-wheeled bikes and e-bikes with sealed dry cell batteries only; no recumbents, tandems, three-wheelers or muddy bikes; fat tires must be deflated to fit; no front-mounted flat racks or folding baskets. You load it yourself. A folding bike can come inside if it stays out of the aisle. On the last trip of the day with a full rack, the driver may let a bike inside. The agency takes no responsibility for damage. Route 20 stops in Guerneville at Safeway and the West County Services Center; weekdays about 12 buses toward Santa Rosa and 10 back, fewer on weekends, when the trips marked Monday to Friday don't run (timetable effective April 12, 2026). The page lists no fare. SMART, the train (policy modified Feb 25, 2026): up to 12 bikes a car, one per rider, space permitting and at the conductor's call; e-bikes need working pedals and a sealed battery and cannot be charged on board; no tandems, three-wheelers, trailers or share bikes; walk the bike on the platform. The policy states no bike fee and no rush-hour rule. The SMART station nearest the airport is a mile from it, at Airport Boulevard and Regional Parkway; the SMART Connect shuttle links the two every day, 8 am to 6 pm, $1.50 (the airport's page, 2026). No train comes closer to Guerneville than Santa Rosa.

bike_share.note: We found no bike share in Guerneville (Nov 2026). Rent from a shop, or stay at one of the three places that keep house bikes for guests.

bring_your_bike.rules_and_safety: California law (Nov 2026). Drivers must give three feet when passing a bike (Vehicle Code 21760); where a second lane runs the same way, the driver moves into it to pass if that is practicable; where three feet is not possible, the driver slows to a reasonable speed and passes only when it does not endanger the rider. The fine is $35, or $220 if a collision injures the rider (statute, Nov 11, 2026). Helmets are required under 18 (21212). E-bikes come in three classes (312.5): class 1 pedal-assist to 20 mph, class 2 throttle to 20 mph, class 3 pedal-assist to 28 mph with a speedometer, rider 16 or older and helmeted. Ride as far right as practicable except when passing, turning left, or in a lane too narrow to share (21202). No earbuds in both ears (27400). At night, a white headlight and a red rear reflector or light (21201). Sidewalk riding is set by each city and county (21206); we couldn't find Sonoma County's rule for unincorporated Guerneville, so walk the bike on Main Street's sidewalks. CalBike's page (modified Aug 24, 2026) lists no stop-as-yield law. The read, from the agencies: Sonoma County Regional Parks, making its case for a separated Lower Russian River Trail, calls the river corridor a "high-traffic, high-speed road with a history of multiple bicycle and pedestrian accidents" with "insufficient sidewalks, bike lanes and no shared use pathways"; that trail is still a proposal with no build date. Caltrans' own Sept 1, 2026 document for Highway 116 from Monte Rio to near Sebastopol lists bike facilities as a top-tier need for the whole corridor. West of town, 116 is down to one lane under temporary signals between Sheridan Ranch Road and Vacation Beach into early 2027 (Caltrans, July 30, 2026); check before a spring trip.

faq.q: Which Guerneville hotels lend bikes to guests?
faq.a: Three say so on their own pages. boon hotel + spa says "We have cruiser bikes available complimentary to our guests," Dawn Ranch offers its "complimentary fleet of Retrospec bikes," and The Stavrand says "Take out one of our cheerful yellow bicycles for a spin (first-come, first-served)." None of them states a policy on bringing your own bike into the room, so ask when you book.

faq.q: What coffee shop in Guerneville opens at 6 a.m.?
faq.a: Coffee Bazaar, downtown at 14045 Armstrong Woods Rd, opens at 6 a.m. every day, Saturday and Sunday included. The Farmhand on River Road opens at 9 and is closed Tuesday and Wednesday, so it's for after the ride.

faq.q: Is there a bike shop in Guerneville, and where is the nearest one?
faq.a: We found no bike shop in Guerneville. The nearest is Russian River Cycle Service at 6559 Front St. in Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line, open Wednesday to Friday 11 to 6 and Saturday 9 to 5 and closed Sunday to Tuesday. Revel Cycles in Sebastopol, about 12 miles southeast in a straight line, is open every day 11 to 6.

faq.q: Where can I rent a bike near the Russian River?
faq.a: We found nothing to rent in Guerneville itself. Russian River Cycle Service in Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line, rents road bikes for $75 a day and hybrids for $45, by appointment seven days a week (Nov 2026). Sports Basement in Santa Rosa has the widest range, with carbon road bikes at $100 a day (chain rates, Nov 2026), and Revel Cycles in Sebastopol rents e-bikes and cruisers only.

faq.q: What bike routes start in or near Guerneville?
faq.a: One loop starts in town: the Sweetwater Springs Road loop, 26 miles and about 2,300 feet, with a climb of 2.3 miles at 8.8%. King Ridge, 55 miles, starts in Monte Rio, and the Sonoma Coast loop, 34 miles, starts in Occidental and passes through Monte Rio. The car-free path is the West County Regional Trail, 5.5 miles each way from Forestville to Sebastopol; it does not reach Guerneville.

faq.q: Where do Cycle to Zero riders sleep in Guerneville?
faq.a: They camp. Cycle to Zero is May 21–23, 2027, and riders camp two nights, Friday and Saturday, May 21 and 22, at Camp Russian River and Johnson's Beach, about a 15-minute walk apart. The hotels in this guide are for whoever drives up to meet a rider.
